Mt. Gox: bitcoin withdrawals halted 7 Feb 2014, closed 25 Feb 2014; about 850,000 BTC reported missing on 28 Feb 2014, 200,000 BTC reported found on 20 Mar 2014, about 650,000 BTC still missing. QuadrigaCX: founder's death announced 14 Jan 2019; more than 76,000 clients owed C$215m, C$46m recovered or identified; an Ontario Securities Commission staff report of 14 Apr 2020 said "Quadriga operated like a Ponzi scheme", staff's view and not a hearing panel's finding. Celsius: withdrawals halted 12 Jun 2022, Chapter 11 on 13 Jul 2022, about $4.7bn owed. Voyager: accounts frozen 1 Jul 2022, customers lost more than $1bn (FTC 12 Oct 2023). FTX: customer withdrawals paused 8 Nov 2022 (SEC complaint), all trading and withdrawals halted 10 Nov 2022, Chapter 11 on 11 Nov 2022, over $8bn of customer deposits missing (CFTC complaint 13 Dec 2022); founder sentenced to 25 years on 28 Mar 2024. Bybit: nearly $1.5bn stolen in February 2025, "the largest digital heist in crypto history" (Chainalysis 8 Jan 2026).

Chainalysis: on-chain scam revenue at least $14bn in 2025 (Chainalysis says the figure could exceed $17bn as it identifies more illicit wallet addresses) after about $12bn in 2024 (revised); total illicit volume 2024 revised to $57.2bn; impersonation scams grew more than 1,400 % in 2025; crypto sent to address-poisoning scams grew more than 15,000 % in 2024, largely from 1 attack in May 2024. US FTC: $15.9bn reported fraud losses in 2025, investment scams $7.9bn (about half), median investment-scam loss $9,196 in 2024. FCA 2025: UK adult crypto ownership fell from 12 % to 8 %; 7 % of UK crypto users say they have personally been a victim of crime, scams, or fraud involving crypto. Patterns with authoritative descriptions: fake investment websites and apps (FTC), unknown exchange platforms (ESAs), pig-butchering (FinCEN alert 8 Sept 2023), fake support and impersonation (ESAs factsheet, December 2025), seed-phrase phishing (ESAs), "guaranteed returns" (FTC: "Only scammers will guarantee profits or big returns"), address poisoning (ESAs; Chainalysis).

CoinGlass on X, 10 Oct 2025 23:48 UTC: "1,618,240 traders were liquidated, with a total liquidation amount of $19.13 billion" in 24 hours, the largest in its dataset; exchanges under-report, so the real figure was likely higher. Liquidations in 2025 to 20 Nov 2025: about $150bn, roughly $400m to $500m a day; first half of 2026: $73.35bn, about $405m a day. ESMA 2018: 74 to 89 % of retail CFD accounts lose money (average losses €1,600 to €29,000); the FCA banned crypto derivatives for retail consumers from 6 Jan 2021.

Portugal taxed crypto gains from 1 Jan 2023 (28 %, 365-day exclusion; Lei 24-D/2022).
Germany raised the private-sales Freigrenze from €600 to €1,000 from tax year 2024 (Wachstumschancengesetz, BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 108).
Italy raised the substitute tax from 26 % to 33 % for gains from 1 Jan 2026 and removed the €2,000 threshold from 2025 (L. 207/2024); euro e-money tokens keep 26 % (L. 199/2025).
Belgium introduced a 10 % tax on gains on financial assets including crypto from 1 Jan 2026 (law of 6 Apr 2026, Moniteur belge 21 Apr 2026).

The UK cut the CGT annual exempt amount from £12,300 to £6,000 for 2023 to 2024 and to £3,000 for 2024 to 2025. From 30 Oct 2024 it raised individuals' main rates, which cover crypto disposals, from 10 % and 20 % to 18 % and 24 %.

Ireland's Budget 2027 cut CGT from 33 % to 31 % for most gains, on disposals from 7 Oct 2026, by Financial Resolution No. 3 of 6 Oct 2026, a Dáil resolution with temporary statutory effect. Section 36 of the Finance (No. 2) Bill 2026 would enact the cut (not enacted on 2 Nov 2026).

alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index: Bitcoin only, 0 to 100, daily data from 1 Feb 2018; 6 inputs as published: volatility 25 %, momentum and volume 25 %, social media 15 %, surveys 15 % (marked "currently paused", redistribution undisclosed), dominance 10 %, Google Trends 10 %. CoinMarketCap's index: launched 3 Aug 2023, 5 components, weights undisclosed ("a complex weighting system"). On 16 Oct 2026 they read 63 "Greed" and 50 "Neutral", 13 points apart on the same day.

FCA InvestSmart (updated 16 May 2025): "Many experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover your outgoings for between 3 and 6 months." BaFin: a rule of thumb of 3 months' income. The CFPB gives no number.

ESAs joint warning 17 Mar 2022: "Consumers face the very real possibility of losing all their invested money"; revised warning 6 Oct 2025: "You may lose a lot, or even all, of the money invested", MiCA protections "not as extensive as those applicable to more traditional financial products (e.g. you will not benefit from compensation schemes)". MiCA Art. 6(5): the asset "may lose its value in part or in full", "may not be liquid", not covered by investor-compensation or deposit-guarantee schemes. FCA COBS 4.12A.11R: "Don't invest unless you're prepared to lose all the money you invest. This is a high-risk investment and you should not expect to be protected if something goes wrong." Central Bank of Ireland: "Consumers could face the possibility of losing all their money if they buy crypto".
